label: START F4
title: Fibre supplement for diverticulosis with a history of constipation
statement: Fibre supplements (e.g., bran, ispaghula, methylcellulose, sterculia) for diverticulosis with a history of constipation.

source.document: O'Mahony D, et al. STOPP/START criteria for potentially inappropriate prescribing in older people: version 3. Eur Geriatr Med 2023;14:625-632, Appendix 1 (corrected supplementary file; NHS Somerset copy used for text, sentence-identical to the earlier parse)
source.citation: O'Mahony D, Cherubini A, Guiteras AR, et al. STOPP/START criteria for potentially inappropriate prescribing in older people: version 3. Eur Geriatr Med 2023;14:625-632. doi:10.1007/s41999-023-00777-y
source.credit: O'Mahony D, Cherubini A, Guiteras AR, et al. STOPP/START criteria for potentially inappropriate prescribing in older people: version 3. Eur Geriatr Med 2023;14:625-632. doi:10.1007/s41999-023-00777-y

plain_summary: A person with small pouches in the bowel wall (diverticulosis) who has had constipation should usually take a fibre supplement to keep the stool soft and easy to pass.

needs_facts.meets: A diagnosis of diverticulosis or diverticular disease is confirmed. A negative answer rules this criterion out. An unknown answer leaves the diagnosis unconfirmed.

Current or past constipation is confirmed. An explicit negative answer rules out this criterion. With confirmed diverticulosis and no recent fibre supplement supply, an unknown history leaves a possible review.

medicine_groups.name: Fibre supplements (medicines that meet this criterion)
medicine_groups.note: Ispaghula husk is also called psyllium husk. Normacol Plus is sterculia with frangula, a stimulant. Bran sold as a food does not usually appear in a dispensing record. Osmotic laxatives such as macrogol and lactulose are not fibre supplements. Generic packs that show the ingredient name with a company name count too. No wheat bran brand is listed in this group.

rule_for_models: Apply this check only to a person aged 65 or over. If age is unknown, establish eligibility before reporting an omission. Make no finding when the record documents a contraindication to the proposed treatment, another valid clinical reason for omitting it, or end-of-life care with a palliative focus. Suspect a finding when the record confirms both diverticulosis and current or past constipation, and no Group A medicine (a fibre supplement) was supplied in the last six months of the record; cite both lines. With diverticulosis recorded, no Group A supply in the last six months and an unknown history of constipation, report only a possible finding. Cite the diverticulosis line and ask whether the person has had constipation. Make no finding if diverticulosis is unconfirmed or a history of constipation is ruled out. If a Group A medicine was supplied in the last six months, there is no finding.
cannot_be_seen: Fibre bought without a prescription, or fibre eaten in food. Also whether a fibre supplement was tried and stopped because of bloating or because it made the constipation worse, and whether a bowel blockage or narrowing rules fibre out.
ask_the_gp: Whether a fibre supplement would help this person's bowel habit, and whether fluids and diet are adequate.
